title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Conduct of Trial Supervision Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Trial Supervision Work

Fa [2004] No. 103

To: All High People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

In accordance with the "Reform Plan for the Internal Structure of the Supreme People's Court" and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretations regarding the functions of its internal departments, the Case Filing Division, the Trial Supervision Division, the Third Civil Division, the Fourth Civil Division, and the Administrative Division of this Court each undertake respective trial supervision functions in relation to corresponding cases. In the course of conducting trial supervision work, in addition to liaison with the relevant business divisions within this Court, liaison is also required with the Case Filing Divisions, Trial Supervision Divisions, and other business divisions of the High People's Courts. Due to the fact that the functional division of internal departments between higher and lower courts is not entirely consistent, certain difficulties have been encountered in coordinating work, which has affected the smooth progress of trial supervision work. In order to earnestly implement the requirement of "justice for the people" and ensure the realization of "fairness and efficiency," and to strengthen trial supervision work, it is hereby notified as follows:

1. For petitions for retrial or applications for retrial that, after review by the relevant business division of this Court, require the High People's Court to reexamine and submit the results of the reexamination, the High People's Court shall conduct the reexamination within the specified time limit and handle the matter in accordance with the law, provide a written reply to the petitioner or the applicant for retrial, and simultaneously submit the results of the reexamination to the relevant business division of this Court.

2. For cases for which the relevant business division of this Court requests the case files, the relevant High People's Court shall send all case files within the specified time limit.

Any other requests made by the relevant business division of this Court based on the actual needs of trial supervision work shall be completed by the High People's Court within the specified time limit.

If, due to special circumstances, a High People's Court is unable to complete the reexamination of cases, the transfer of case files, or other matters as specified above within the time limit, it shall explain the circumstances to the relevant business division of this Court before the expiration of the time limit and propose the expected time for completion.

3. For cases in which this Court instructs the High People's Court to conduct a retrial and communicates specific issues in writing, the High People's Court shall, after rendering its judgment, promptly submit the judgment document to the Supreme People's Court.

4. The various relevant business divisions of this Court, in carrying out trial supervision work in accordance with their respective duties and responsibilities, are all exercising the trial supervision authority on behalf of this Court. The relevant business divisions of the High People's Courts that undertake trial supervision tasks shall, with a highly responsible attitude, each perform their own duties, actively assist and cooperate with the relevant business divisions of this Court in properly handling the work related to petitions and applications for retrial as well as trial supervision work. They shall not shirk their responsibilities or cause delays on the grounds that the business departments of the higher and lower courts do not correspond.

5. If the above requirements are violated, the relevant business division of this Court shall actively supervise and urge compliance; if no improvement is made after such supervision, this Court will handle the matter in accordance with the relevant provisions.

May 18, 2004
